Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Ireland's reply with the bat. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Amy Hunter and Alana Dalzell open up for Ireland Women. Marizanne Kapp starts with the new ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Enough on the board? So, 137 is what Ireland need to get a win in this warm-up, but they will be up against a finely synced South African bowling unit. The new-ball phase becomes really crucial for the Irish women to set a strong foundation and build a strong base for their chase. The conditions are overcast, and batting is not as straightforward as Wolvaardt made it look like. The target might look a modest one, but they will have to bat well here.

Irish bowlers boss it up later - Wolvaardt brought up a fine half century and formed a couple of handy partnerships along the way, with her stand alongside Annerie Dercksen doing particularly well to stabilise the innings. But the moment she was dismissed, South Africa collapsed in a heap, sliding from 113/2 to 135/8 in no time, and couldn't find the final push to get past 150. Ireland used as many as seven bowlers. They took a bit of a tap initially, but solidly bounced back through the likes of Arlene Kelly, who picked up a spectacular three-for, while Ava Canning and Cara Murray picked up two apiece to twist the knife further.

The Proteas start brightly - Overcast conditions greeted both sides, with the seamers finding some assistance in the air and off the pitch. South Africa's openers made a bright start regardless, helping themselves to the loose balls on offer. Luus was the first to go, but Wolvaardt looked pristine at the other end. Maguire removed Brits to make it two down, yet Wolvaardt kept going. Ireland steadied themselves through the middle phase, reeling off some quiet overs to peg South Africa back at 59/2.

Good finish with the ball - Excellent execution in the final few overs by the Irish bowlers. They just choked the Proteas and conceded just 20 runs in the last 4 overs and, more importantly, kept picking up wickets regularly to expose the tail. South Africa, on the other hand, would be a bit disappointed with the score they have posted. They were cruising nicely with Wolvaardt in the middle, but couldn't build on the foundation she laid and lost their way in the death, leaving a few loose ends to address before the big tournament.

With five overs to go, since it is an 18-over per side contest, they will look to put the foot down for a huge total, in excess of 160. Ireland will be desperate to break this stand as quickly as possible. Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are all set for the action to begin. The two umpires make their way out in the middle. The Irish women are huddled near the ropes. They now make their way in the middle as well and take their respective field positions. Sune Luus and Laura Wolvaardt open up for the South Africa Women. Aimee Maguire will start with the new ball. Also, this will be an 18-over per side contest. Let's go...

Pitch Report -  Shebani Bhaskar is pitchside. She informs that it is gloomy and brighter right now. Notes that the outfield looks lush green and well-manicured. Informs that there is some possibility of rain later in the day as well. On the surface, she points out that it was under covers all night, and it is pretty damp and cold to touch. She expects some movement off the surface and through the air for the seamers. Stresses that the spinners should keep the attack on the stumps to get success on this track.

South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Sune Luus, Annerie Dercksen, Chloe Tryon, Dane Van Niekerk, Karabo Meso, Kayla Reyneke, Marizanne Kapp, Nadine De Klerk, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Ayabonga Khaka, Nonkululeko Mlaba, Shabnim Ismail, Tumi Sekhukhune.

Ireland Women - Amy Hunter (WK), Arlene Kelly, Christina Coulter Reilly, Gaby Lewis (C), Lara McBride, Laura Delany, Leah Paul, Louise Little, Orla Prendergast, Rebecca Stokell, Aimee Maguire, Alana Dalzell, Ava Canning, Cara Murray, Georgina Dempsey.

The skipper of South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt says that they have spent a lot of time bowling first, so they are happy to bat now. She adds that they have spent a lot of time together as a team, and they have a lot of talent on their side. She reckons that it is about playing a good game and ends by saying that they will give their best in this tournament.

The skipper of Ireland Women - Gaby Lewis says that they will bowl first. Adds that it is because of the rain, and they will try to chase the target. Adds that they had a great tri-series, and they will carry on with the same momentum. She ends by saying that they will try to keep it going and stay positive.
TOSS - Ireland Women have won the toss, and they will BOWL first.

What's cooking at Lord's? Since the weather is holding us up here, why don't we dive into the drama happening at the Home of Cricket? England are firmly in the driving seat after a sensational day with both bat and ball, leaving New Zealand facing a massive uphill task under these gloomy, overcast London skies. It’s 'Moving Day' in that series opener, and we could see a swift conclusion. New Zealand find themselves in a massive spot of bother at 36/3, needing a further 218 runs to chase down their 254-run target, while England hunt just 7 wickets to secure a clinical victory. That action will start soon, so you could switch tabs and enjoy the coverage of that game as well.

UPDATE - 8.54 am GMT - Live visuals show that it is raining right now and the covers are firmly placed on the pitch and the squares. Ground staff are out in numbers, sweeping water off the sheets, while one of the umpires has an umbrella up as she takes a look at the conditions, and is seen having a chat with the head of the ground staff. The conditions are very gloomy out there. Alan Wilkins on air mentions that the skies aren't looking as angry as they were an hour ago. He also informs that there was heavy overnight rain in Loughborough, but feels confident that some cricket will be played eventually. Let's stay optimistic as Wilko is. Stay tuned.

TOSS DELAYED - Not an official word, though, but since the conditions are overcast with a bit of rain around, it looks like the coin flip has been delayed in Loughborough. We will get right back the moment we get an official update. Stay tuned.

Recent form - South Africa have had a mixed bag of 2026 so far, winning 7 and losing 6 T20Is. Whereas Ireland have won 7 out of 10 T20Is this year. While the Irish face a stern challenge against a side like South Africa, it is a perfect opportunity for them to test their skills before the World Cup starts. Toss and other updates coming up shortly. Stay tuned.

Ireland are ready to challenge - Ireland, placed in Group B, booked their spot in this mega event through the ICC Women's T20 World Cup Global Qualifier earlier this year. Led by the experienced Gaby Lewis, the Irish side has shown considerable growth and resilience in the shortest format and would look to translate that into the global event.

The Proteas arrive with momentum - Drawn into a highly competitive Group A (alongside Australia, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands), South Africa will be eager to use this warm-up fixture to solidify their combinations. The Proteas come into the tournament with impressive momentum, having recently secured a dominant 4-1 T20I series victory over India in April 2026.

Time for the warm-ups - The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 is just around the corner, and the warm-up matches offer teams a final opportunity to fine-tune their strategies and acclimatise to the English conditions. In Match 2 of the warm-ups, South Africa Women will take on Ireland Women at the Haslegrave Cricket Ground.
